Display/Regular/M.description: A slightly more restrained hero size. For prominent page or section openers that still need presence but sit alongside other content, or as the Display L replacement on narrower desktop layouts.

Display/Regular/L.description: The largest type in the scale. For single high-impact moments — marketing hero headlines, splash/landing sections, or big promotional numbers — where one short line needs to dominate the screen. Desktop only; step down on smaller breakpoints.

Display/Medium/S.description: The entry point to the display range, bridging into the Headline scale below it. For feature headers, campaign banners, and emphasis moments that need to feel larger than a standard headline without going full hero.

Shadows/Extra Small.description: The lowest elevation — a tight, barely-there shadow. For elements that need to lift off the background just slightly: input fields, tags, or subtle dividers between surfaces.

Shadows/Base.value: drop shadow: offset 0/5 blur 12 color #000000 (5%) | drop shadow: offset 0/2 blur 8 color #000000 (8%)
Shadows/Base.description: The default resting elevation for most raised surfaces — standard cards, list items, and containers sitting on a page. The everyday shadow when a component just needs to feel grounded.

Background Blur/Small.description: The lightest frost. Gently softens whatever sits behind an element while keeping it recognisable — good for subtle glass effects on floating bars, sticky headers, or chips layered over content.

Shadows/Medium.value: drop shadow: offset 0/6 blur 12 color #000000 (8%) | drop shadow: offset 0/4 blur 16 color #000000 (5%)
Shadows/Medium.description: A step up for interactive or temporarily raised surfaces — hover/active card states, dropdowns, and popovers. Signals that an element is above its neighbours.

Background Blur/Medium.description: A moderate blur that noticeably obscures the background without fully hiding it. Suited to popovers, dropdowns, and smaller panels where you want depth and a frosted feel but still hint at the content underneath.

Shadows/XLarge.description: The highest elevation. Reserved for the most prominent overlays — modals, dialogs, and bottom sheets — where a strong, soft shadow separates them from everything behind.

Background Blur/XLarge.description: A heavy blur that reduces the background to soft colour and shape. For full-screen scrims and modal backdrops where the goal is to pull focus firmly onto the foreground layer.

Background Blur/XXLarge.description: The strongest blur — the background becomes an abstract wash of colour. Reserved for the most immersive overlays, onboarding takeovers, or loading/transition states where the content behind should all but disappear.

Shadows/Large.value: drop shadow: offset 0/10 blur 20 color #000000 (12%) | drop shadow: offset 0/4 blur 6 color #000000 (2%)
Shadows/Large.description: For floating overlays that clearly detach from the page — menus, tooltips, date pickers, and toasts. Noticeably deeper to read as on top of the content below.
